Here is the data and context you need to write the thread:

        MARKET DATA:
        - ASX 200 closed last week at 8,522 points
        - The ASX 200 is up 1.2% for the month so far
        - RBA held rates at 3.85% at its September meeting
        - Australian CPI (monthly indicator) came in at 2.7% for August (released last week)
        - Iron ore spot price: USD 98.50 per tonne
        - Gold: USD 3,320 per oz
        - Brent crude: USD 74.20 per barrel
        - AUD/USD: 0.6485
        - S&P 500 closed at 5,702 points last week
        - US Fed held rates at 4.25–4.50% at its September FOMC meeting
        - US 10-year Treasury yield: 4.18%
        - Key events this week: Australian unemployment data (Thursday), US PCE inflation (Friday)

        SECTOR/STOCK CONTEXT:
        - Banks: RBA on hold, net interest margin pressure easing, sector up 3.1% past month
        - Mining: iron ore sub-USD 100/t, China stimulus hopes fading, sector lagging
        - Gold stocks: benefiting from USD 3,320/oz gold price, sector outperforming YTD
        - Energy: Brent at USD 74.20/bbl, sector under pressure from soft demand outlook
        - Property/REITs: rate hold supportive, watching unemployment data closely
        - Macquarie Group: reporting earnings this week, consensus expects flat result

Post 1

ASX 200 at 8,522 — CPI at 2.7% clears the air but the RBA at 3.85% stays anchored. Mixed stance this week: rate relief is priced, now earnings and jobs data decide if the rally has legs. #ASX #ausbiz #RBA

Post 2

🏦 Banks up 3.1% past month — NIM pressure easing with RBA on hold. 🪙 Gold stocks outperforming YTD with bullion at USD 3,320/oz. Two sectors with real momentum heading into a data-heavy week. #ASX #banking #gold

Post 3

📉 Iron ore at USD 98.50/t — sub-100 is a line in the sand for miners. China stimulus hopes fading fast. Watch the mining sector for a flush if spot breaks lower this week. #ASX #mining #ironore

Post 4

S&P 500 closed at 5,702 with the Fed on hold at 4.25–4.50%. US 10-year at 4.18% keeps pressure on rate-sensitive ASX plays. AUD/USD 0.6485 — any USD strength hits commodity names hard. #ASX #ausbiz #Fed

Post 5

Friday's US PCE is the week's sharpest risk. A hot print pressures the Fed and lifts the USD — bad for AUD and local equities. A soft read opens the door for risk-on. Thursday AU jobs data adds a local wildcard. Which way are you positioned? #ASX #ausbiz #inflation
